summary: Tells git which files never to track: local secrets, the runtime database and Python tool caches. Everything listed is either private or regenerated automatically, so the repository holds only source code and configuration.

notes.text: Section comment: local configuration and secrets.
The real `.env` file may hold the API key and an OpenAI key, so it must never be committed; `.env.example` is the shareable template.
Section comment: runtime data. The database is created and seeded on first start, so there is nothing worth committing.

The top-level `data/` folder, where `iip/config.py` places the default SQLite database. The leading slash anchors the rule to the repository root: a bare `data/` would also ignore `web/js/data/`, which holds the world map's dot mask, so a fresh clone would have shown a broken map.
Any SQLite database file, wherever it ends up.

SQLite's companion files: `-wal` is the write-ahead log and `-shm` its shared-memory index. They exist because `iip/database.py` switches SQLite to WAL mode so the live-traffic writer and the dashboard readers can work at the same time.
The local virtual environment (the installed packages), which is large and specific to one machine.
Compiled bytecode that Python writes automatically when it imports modules.
pytest's cache (for example, which tests failed on the last run).
